BY ADV SRI.PREMCHAND M.- SC  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY  HEARD ON 06.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE

FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 513 OF 2016 3  2025:KER:11785  JUDGMENT Dated this the 6th day of February, 2025
The claimants in O.P.(M.V.) No. 1073/ 2012 on the file of the I st Addl.
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kollam,
are the appellants herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the wife and children of the deceased Unnikrishnan, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 10.05.2012.

According to them, on 10.05.2012, at about 10.30 a.m, while the deceased was travelling in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No. KL-24/0711, a Maruthi ZEN car bearing Reg.No. KL-03/J 4167,
driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against motorcycle of the deceased and as a result of which he fell down and sustained serious injuries and later on he succumbed to the injuries, on 14.05.2012, while under treatment.
3.
The 1st respondent is the owner , the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:11785 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs. 10,00,000/-.
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PW1 and PW2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A9.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

Geethakumari vs Zachariah(Deleted) on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59210307/
2 6.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,91,607/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

9. Heard Sri S. Santhosh Kumar, the learned Counsel appearing for the claimants/appellants, and Sri. M. Premchand, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of 2025:KER:11785 the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the deceased was working as Heavy vehicle driver earning Rs. 8000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5500/-.
11. It is true that the petitioner could not prove his income, as claimed in the OP.
However from Ext.A8 driving licence it is proved that the petitioner was a driver by profession.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner being a driver by profession, his notional income is fixed at Rs.10000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.
12. On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 46 years.

Therefore, 25 % of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was married who left behind three dependants, towards personal and 2025:KER:11785 living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.13,00,000/-.
13.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.5000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.50,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and each dependent is entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.
Towards loss of consortium, petitioners 1 to 3 together are entitled to get a sum of Rs. 1,45,200/- (48,400 x 3).

3 14.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.

New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.

15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has 2025:KER:11785 awarded Rs.10,000/-,
which according to the learned counsel for the petitioners, is on the lower side.
The deceased died in this case 4 days after the accident.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lower side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
16.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

17. Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.15,26,055/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

4 deposited, if any, along with interest @8% per annum, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

19. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
